Seminar Title:

A Comparative Study on Mechanical and Wear Behaviour of Al7075 Metal Matrix Composites Fabricated by Additive Manufacturing and Powder Metallurgy

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Mechanical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Dhira Shankar Patra ( Rollno : 524me1007)

Abstract:

Now-a-days, Alumimium alloys are widely preferred over traditional materials like steel and copper as they offer an exceptional strength-to-weight ratio and high corrosion resistance. Al7075 is a high-strength aluminum alloy primarily grouped within the 7xxx series, where zinc is the primary alloying element, alongside magnesium and copper. It is widely recognized for its excellent wear and corrosion resistance, high strength, ease of fabrication, and heat-treatable nature. In addition to their mechanical performance, the tribological behaviour of Al alloys including friction, wear, and surface damage plays a crucial role in determining their reliability and service life under sliding and contact conditions. Although various traditional manufacturing routes are available, powder metallurgy (PM) is most commonly used to fabricate aluminum alloy parts, even though it faces challenges regarding geometric complexity and processing limits. In contrast, additive manufacturing (AM) technologies have advanced rapidly, shifting from simple prototyping methods to highly capable manufacturing alternatives. Choosing AM over PM to produce Al7075 parts provides a critical advantage if your application demands extreme geometric complexity, customized low-volume production, or functional design integration. The present study investigates the mechanical and dry sliding wear behaviour of Al7075 alloy fabricated via laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) based AM and PM technique. This study aims tofind the relationships between fabrication methods, structural characteristics, and the resulting mechanical and wear behavior. Five samples were fabricated using PM at different compaction pressures such as 375MPa, 500MPa, 625MPa, 750MPa and 875MPa, respectively and sintered. The influence of compaction pressure and sintering temperature on the mechanical properties of Al7075 alloy made by powder metallurgy route was investigated in the preliminary investigation. The dense part with least porosity was found at the compaction pressure of 625 MPa. Al7075 alloy parts were successfully produced via LPBF. Experiments were conducted based on Taguchi's L9 orthogonal array design. The process parameters like such as laser power (140 W, 240 W and 340 W), scan speed (500 mm/s, 900 mm/s and 1300 mm/s), layer thickness (0.03 mm, 0.035 mm and 0.04 mm), and hatch spacing (0.09 mm, 0.11 mm and 0.13 mm) were considered for optimization. The spherical morphology of the Al7075 powder particles, as confirmed by SEM, is expected to enhance both powder flowability and packing density during LPBF. Consequently, this optimized powder bed quality can improve the mechanical and wear properties of the fabricated components. The chemical composition of the Al7075 alloy was verified using EDX analysis.
